Guidance & outlook: Based on our current order book, execution pipeline, and opportunities across existing and new business verticals, we are targeting revenue growth of approximately 50% to 60% over FY27 and FY28, while maintaining margin discipline and improving working capital efficiency.
EBITDA for FY26 stood at INR22.1 crores, while EBITDA margins remained healthy at approximately 15.4% as against 17.1% in FY25.
Profit after tax for FY26 stood at INR13.1 crores, compared to INR9.1 crores in FY25, reflecting a growth of 43% year -on-year.
Growth & demand: As of March '26, our order book stood at a pproximately INR 323 crores across 13 projects.

Starting with the second half of performance, revenue for H2 during financial year '26 stood at INR78.20 crores as against INR72.4 crores in the previous financial year H2 FY25, reflecting a 8% year-on-year growth.
With an INR323 crore of order book as of 31 March, 2026 and INR447 crores order book as on 15 May, 2026.
Margins & costs: Alongside Surapet pr oject, we secured INR40.5 Crores Odour control system contract from CMWSSB, covering 46 sewage pumping stations across Chennai, including design, engineering, commissioning, and five years O&M component.
EBITDA for this period stood at INR13.7 crores with EBITDA margins at approximately 17.5% for the H2 period.
As WTP operations stabilizes and scale up, we believe the EBITDA margins in the 15% to 16% range remains sustainable.
Capex & expansion: One of our key projects under execution is design, build, operate, and transfer of 47 MLD water treatment plant in Surapet, Chennai for CMWSSB, valued at INR106 crores, including 10 years O&M component.

We are also executing the STP project for Hosur City Municipal Corporation in Krishnagiri district, comprising 12.5 MLD and 20.1 MLD capacity using Sequential Batch Reactor technology, and valued at approximately INR107 Crores.
In that order, INR100 crores is towards the capex.
Balance sheet & cash: We are encouraged by the collection momentum post year -end, and approximately about 33% of receivables have already been collected by the end of May 2026.
During FY26, trade receivables stood at INR49.5 crores as of March 2026.

Encouragingly, approximately 33% of these receivables have already been collected post year-end, and out of which 50% will be received in the next week and remaining balance will be realized before the end of June.
Risks & challenges: We don't see any slowdown because we have intention to move geographically.
So we don't find any change other than expecting the delay in new tendering process.
This capital work in progress, now we are going for an enhanced software.
